prompt:
Pixel-art sprite sheet, single image, fully transparent background.

SUBJECT: the anthropomorphic monkey basketball player in the attached reference
image. Match that character exactly, his face above all: a lean, wiry,
long-armed ape with dark brown fur all over, a thick shaggy mop of spiky darker
fur on his head, and a DARK ape face exactly as the reference draws it -- a
heavy brow ridge, small deep-set eyes under it with a stern, intense stare, a
broad flat nose and a wide thin-lipped mouth, the skin of the face a darker
brown, NOT a pale cartoon muzzle; small ears set close to the head. Long
muscular arms with big hands, a long curling tail. A blue sleeveless basketball
jersey with a yellow number 7, blue shorts with white and yellow trim,
blue-and-white high-top sneakers. Identical colours, identical proportions,
identical build and identical height as the reference, in every frame.

LAYOUT: one horizontal row of 4 frames of equal width, evenly spaced. No
borders, no frame numbers, no labels, no background, no drop shadows.

POSE GUIDE: TWO images are attached, and they do different jobs.

The COLOUR image of the character is the only authority on WHO HE IS. His
colours, his proportions, his build, his height, his face, his kit and the
drawing style all come from that image and from the SUBJECT above, and nothing
below changes any of them. It does NOT decide which way he faces: in this sheet
he faces the viewer.

The other image is a POSE GUIDE: a stick figure on a white background, standing
in a row on one ground line, in the same left-to-right order as the FRAMES
listed below. The Nth figure in the pose guide is the pose for the Nth frame.
Take the GEOMETRY from it and only the geometry: where each foot stands, how
deeply the knees are bent, how low the shoulders and head are, and where the
elbows and hands are.

THE COLOURS ON THE POSE GUIDE name the limbs: the RED arm and the ORANGE leg
are on the VIEWER'S LEFT, the BLUE arm and the GREEN leg on the viewer's right.

THE HANDS ON THE POSE GUIDE: the FLAT hand with its fingers spread sideways is
palm-down; a narrow shape pointing down is a hand hanging loose; a small
rounded square is a clenched FIST.

THE HEAD ON THE POSE GUIDE: the small TRIANGLE is his nose and the two ovals
his ears; his face points at the viewer.

Draw the character from the colour reference standing in those positions. The
pose guide is an instruction, not artwork: its thin lines, its colours, its
joint dots, its white background, its circular head, its triangle, its ovals
and its face lines are NOT part of the drawing and must not appear anywhere in
it.

CAMERA: locked off. Identical distance and eye level in every frame. The
character must be exactly the same height in every frame, and the same height
as in the reference image — do not zoom, crop, recompose or rescale between
frames. All frames share one ground line: the soles of the feet touch the same
horizontal line in every frame. The feet stay planted throughout.

VIEW: front view, facing the viewer, squared to camera, starting from the low
athletic dribbling stance.

An opponent has just knocked the ball out of his hands. Frames 2 to 4 are one
continuous reaction, pure monkey: half a beat of surprise, then a bewildered,
very ape-like scratch and pluck at the fur on the top of his own head, then
straight back into his stance.

FRAMES, left to right:
1. CALIBRATION POSE: standing straight upright, feet shoulder-width apart, arms
   hanging relaxed at his sides, facing the viewer, in the plain neutral
   standing pose from the reference image. This exact pose appears as the first
   frame of every sheet in this set and must be drawn identically every time.
2. The instant it goes: still crouched low in the dribbling stance, the
   dribbling hand (on the viewer's LEFT) still out with the palm down over
   nothing at all, head snapped down toward where the ball was, eyes wide open
   and both brows up, mouth dropped open. His tail shooting straight up in
   surprise.
3. The pluck: half upright, knees still bent and a little bowed, the arm on the
   VIEWER'S RIGHT raised with the elbow cocked out high to the side and the
   fingers on the very TOP of his head, scratching and plucking at the shaggy
   fur on his crown the way a real monkey does. The other arm hangs long and
   loose, knuckles low. Head tipped to one side, eyebrows up, lips pushed out
   in a puzzled "ooh" pout, eyes darting about for where the ball went. A few
   tufts of fur stick up where he is plucking. His tail curled up in a question
   mark behind him.
4. Back in his stance: crouched again, feet a little wider than his shoulders,
   the hand on the VIEWER'S LEFT held out palm-down at hip height as if
   dribbling, the other arm hanging, still frowning in puzzlement, the fur on
   his crown still ruffled -- exactly his dribbling stance at the top of the
   bounce. His tail hanging in a relaxed curl.

This is a one-shot, not a loop. Frame 2 must continue naturally from the low
athletic dribbling stance, and frame 4 settles back into that same stance.

The three frames must differ clearly in what the hands are doing: crouched with
the hand low over nothing, one hand up on the top of his head, then the stance
with the hand at hip height. No basketball is drawn in any frame: the game
draws it separately.

STYLE: VGA-era 256-colour DOS-game pixel art, drawn pixel by pixel — NOT a
modern illustration with a pixel filter over it. The limits below are the look;
keep all of them: - At most THREE tones per material: a base, one darker
shadow, one lighter highlight. Hard edges between the tones. - NO gradients, NO
soft or airbrushed shading, NO glow, NO bloom, and NO anti-aliasing anywhere —
not on the outline, not between tones, not around the silhouette. - Where a
tone change needs softening, use visible ORDERED DITHER — a checkerboard of the
two tones. Dither, never blend. - Chunky square pixels on one consistent grid,
plainly visible at full size. - A bold dark outline around the silhouette and
around the major forms inside it. The background must be fully transparent
(alpha 0) with no haze, glow or soft fringe around the silhouette. Output a
wide landscape image.

The character is NOT holding a basketball in any frame — the ball is drawn
separately by the game.
